newsitem.title: GERMANY: Trichet - deficit key to EMU, welcomes French efforts.
newsitem.headline: Trichet - deficit key to EMU, welcomes French efforts.

text.p: A sustainably low budget deficit will be key for entry to European monetary union, Bank of France governor Jean-Claude Trichet said on Thursday, cautiously welcoming France's efforts to cut its shortfall.

Trichet told Germany's Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung: "The Banque de France can only welcome the fact that Finance Minister (Dominique) Strauss-Kahn has presented a comprehensive plan for the reduction of the deficit. This was necessary and it is good that it has been agreed."
"...I trust in the will of the French government, and the German government, to fulfil the treaty and the 3-percent goal," Trichet said.
He added however that it was not the position of the French central bank to comment in detail on the measures set by Paris.

Turning to the general question of how countries will be selected for participation in EMU, Trichet said it was clear that the fiscal criteria calling for a deficit to be no more than three percent of total output would play an important role.

Asked to comment on the discussion in Germany as to whether the word three stated in the Masstricht treaty must be interpreted to mean 3.0 percent, Trichet said there could be no change to the treaty at this stage and its wording was the basis for decision.
"It is not up to me to pass judgement on the public discussion in Germany," he said. "I would simply like to say that I am convinced that the treaty must be implemented in its current version.

"And I am convinced that the most important criterion at the time of the decision will be whether the reduction of the deficits is sustainable or not. It will be decisive whether the budget plans for 1998 and 1999 are credible," he added.

Trichet ruled out a delay in the start of European monetary union, adding that French lawyers did not believe this would be possible under the terms of the Maastricht Treaty. Renegotiation of the treaty coud threaten the whole project.
